crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers include interface design, systems integration and shared software solution work relevant to API/platform engineering, but the occupation is broader than this platform specialization.

crosswalks.label: Computer Systems Engineers/Architects
crosswalks.rationale: Systems Engineers/Architects contribute complex application and systems-integration work relevant to platform boundaries without defining API/platform engineering as a whole profession.

findings.summary: O*NET occupational evidence supports software interface, integration and reusable systems work that forms part of API/platform engineering, while no single occupation cleanly equals the AXM package boundary.
findings.rationale: The body reconstructs explicit API contracts, compatibility, platform abstraction and consumer migration while retaining narrower ownership.

findings.summary: Compatibility tooling can identify affected consumers and breakage surfaces but should not decide each consuming domain's semantic migration or product tradeoff.
method_labels: O*NET occupation comparison plus AXM body-boundary review
findings.rationale: Platform work crosses many consumers; explicit authority separation prevents shared infrastructure from becoming silent domain governance.

gaps_against_body.description: Add explicit rule that compatibility tooling may identify affected consumers but cannot decide a consuming domain's semantic migration for it.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of API / Platform Engineer.
O*NET occupation mappings are human-work evidence, not AXM profession identity or authority transfer.
